what: secondary analysis (not the pre-registered comparison of that run): float64 value-and-gradient of mean-square operator residuals of one-hidden-layer ridge networks; XLA closed-form programs vs structure-aware and network-level Taylor-mode AD
hardware: one NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB (exclusive), JAX 0.10.2 with jaxlib 0.10.2 CUDA 12 plugins, CPython 3.12

protocol.repetitions: 3 fresh processes (paired by repetition, rotating method order)
protocol.statistic: ratio = strongest-control median / candidate median per tier; lower95 = exp(mean(log r) - 2.920 sd(log r)/sqrt(3)); strongest control = smallest mean log median among qualified tier members
protocol.qualification: every compared method: loss and gradients vs 40-digit mpmath on a row subset (gradients atol 1e-8 / rtol 2e-9, values 1e-9 / 2e-10, scaled); full-size outputs finite and digest-checked

status.parity: lower95 < 1 <= ratio or ratio < 1 <= upper bound
status.partial: an applicable tier member failed (e.g. out of memory) or did not qualify; never promoted

protocol.fairness: identical data, initialisation, loss and float64 inputs for every method; compilation excluded (value-and-gradient steady state)

tiers.taylor_structure_aware: Taylor mode in the ridge variable z per hidden unit, combined with exact operator-symbol amplitudes (exploits the one-layer ridge structure)
tiers.taylor_network_level: network-level higher-order AD of u(x): JAX Taylor mode (jet) and collapsed Taylor mode along exact polarization directions (run when <= 400 directions), nested forward-mode AD per monomial (run when the monomial work is bounded), folx forward Laplacian (Delta to Delta^3 only)

candidates.struct_closed: autodiff of the tanh closed-form symbol for general multi-index operators (no shipped module; reported because it loses)
